metadata.title: Cross-Substrate Sequential-Grammar Pipeline Recovers Alpha-Suppression Topography in Human EEG: Convergent Validation on Mental Arithmetic Recordings
metadata.description: We test whether the substrate-agnostic sequential-grammar pipeline previously validated on superconducting quantum-processor readouts and on large-language-model logit-entropy traces also recovers state-discriminative information from human EEG. Using an unmodified pipeline (SAX alphabet K=7, LSTM hidden_dim=16, seq_len=20, 50 epochs), we analyze 36 healthy volunteers' eyes-closed rest versus first-minute mental arithmetic recordings (19-channel 10-20 montage; PhysioNet eegmat 1.0.0). Per-stream grammar perplexity discriminates regimes with Cohen's d = 0.99 (Wilcoxon p = 9.1e-83); the spatial distribution recapitulates the classical Berger-Klimesch alpha-suppression topography; leave-one-subject-out classification of regime achieves 75.2% accuracy on held-out subjects. AAFT surrogate analysis indicates that the discrimination is mediated by linear power-spectral content re-represented as symbolic grammar (regime x surrogate interaction n.s.). Convergent validation that the same pipeline used across two prior substrates (quantum and linguistic) recovers substrate-appropriate, neurophysiologically interpretable state distinctions in human EEG.
references: Berger, H. (1929). Über das Elektrenkephalogramm des Menschen. Archiv für Psychiatrie und Nervenkrankheiten, 87, 527-570.
Klimesch, W. (1999). EEG alpha and theta oscillations reflect cognitive and memory performance. Brain Research Reviews, 29, 169-195.
Theiler, J., Eubank, S., Longtin, A., Galdrikian, B. & Farmer, J. D. (1992). Testing for nonlinearity in time series: the method of surrogate data. Physica D, 58, 77-94.
Lin, J., Keogh, E., Wei, L. & Lonardi, S. (2007). Experiencing SAX: a novel symbolic representation of time series. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery, 15(2), 107-144.
Zyma, I., Tukaev, S., Seleznov, I., Kiyono, K., Popov, A., Chernykh, M. & Shpenkov, O. (2019). Electroencephalograms during Mental Arithmetic Task Performance. Data, 4(1), 14.
